9.0.s.en: 1. Heads of fathers from the captivity

9.0.0.en: 1 So all Israel were reckoned by genealogies; and, behold, they were written in the book of the kings of Israel. And Judah was carried away to Babylon for their transgression. 2 Now the first inhabitants that dwelt in their possessions in their cities were Israel, the priests, Levites, and the Nethinims. 3 And in Jerusalem dwelt of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin, and of the children of Ephraim, and Manasseh; 4 Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, of the children of Pharez the son of Judah. 5 And of the Shilonites; Asaiah the firstborn, and his sons. 6 And of the sons of Zerah; Jeuel, and their brethren, six hundred and ninety. 7 And of the sons of Benjamin; Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hasenuah, 8 And Ibneiah the son of Jeroham, and Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri, and Meshullam the son of Shephathiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah; 9 And their brethren, according to their generations, nine hundred and fifty and six. All these men were chief of the fathers in the house of their fathers.

9.0.1.en: So all Israel were reckoned by genealogies; and, behold, they were written in the book of the kings of Israel.

9.0.2.en: And Judah was carried away to Babylon for their transgression. [1]

9.0.3.en: Here he looks back to the genealogies mentioned before, and tells us that they were gathered from the books of the kings of Israel and Judah, not those books included in the Bible, but in the civil records, which are reliable records.

9.0.4.en: With man's personal responsibility for his works, he must also pray for the sanctification of the community as a whole, so that God's wrath may not come upon all.

9.0.5.en: All Israel: here Israel together with Judah is meant.

9.0.6.en: The captivity took place because of the people's fall as a whole into idol worship, despite the Lord's continual warnings to them through the prophets.

9.0.7.en: Even those of them who had not turned aside to idol worship were exposed to falling into the captivity. Therefore it befits the believer to cry to God in repentance and return to Him, not for himself or his family only, but for the whole community as well. Truly we are not judged for the sins of others, even if they are the closest to us, but in love we must desire, ask for and do whatever we can for the salvation of all.

9.1.0.en: Now the first inhabitants that dwelt in their possessions in their cities were Israel, the priests, Levites, and the Nethinims. [2]

9.1.1.en: The first inhabitants: most likely meaning those who were first in the return from the captivity, because this chapter resembles the eleventh chapter of Nehemiah.

9.1.2.en: They are Israel, the priests, etc. That is, the people and the priests, etc.

9.1.3.en: The Nethinim: a Hebrew name meaning "dedicated". It occurs in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah, and it means the Gentiles who were assigned to the service of the Temple, such as the Gibeonites (Josh 9:3, 27), and the Midianite captives (Num 31:2, 47), and those whom David appointed with the princes for the service of the Temple and the service of the Levitical priests (Ezra 8:20), and they were hewers of wood and drawers of water. Although David is the one who established the office of the Nethinim, it is thought that the name attached to them later, and the name occurs only in the days of Nehemiah and Ezra, and once in First Chronicles (1 Chr 9:2). The number of the Nethinim was not sufficient to perform all the services of the Temple, especially in the days of Solomon.

9.2.0.en: And in Jerusalem dwelt of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin, and of the children of Ephraim, and Manasseh; [3]

9.2.1.en: The most important of those returning from the captivity were the tribes of Judah and Benjamin (Ezra 1:5).

9.2.2.en: Jerusalem: it was not a part of the Promised Land in the time of Joshua son of Nun, and it was not distributed among the tribes, but remained in the possession of the Canaanites and particularly the Jebusites, and was called "Jebus". It was a fortified city, difficult to storm. David's forces were able to storm it in 992 BC, and David made it the capital of the kingdom (2 Sam 5:6-7). For this reason we find that the city of Jerusalem, unlike the rest of the cities, was inhabited by Israelites from many tribes [3].

9.2.3.en: Since the ark of the covenant was carried to it after it became the capital, Jerusalem became a religious center, and after the building of the Temple in the days of Solomon it became a dwelling for many priests and Levites and other liturgical servants [10-12].

9.2.4.en: By the sons of Benjamin and the sons of Ephraim and Manasseh are meant people from these tribes near Jerusalem in the north, who worshipped the Lord and united with Judah (2 Chr 30:10, 18).

9.3.0.en: Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, of the children of Pharez the son of Judah. [4]

9.3.1.en: Uthai (Utai): a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah surpassed". It is the name of a son of Ammihud, of the sons of Pharez son of Judah. He was one of those who returned to Jerusalem after the captivity (1 Chr 9:4).

9.3.2.en: Ammihud: a Hebrew name, meaning "my uncle is majestic". He was the son of Omri, one of the descendants of Pharez, of the sons of Judah; his son Uthai returned to Jerusalem after the captivity (1 Chr 9:4).

9.3.3.en: Omri: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "prosperous". He was the son of Imri son of Pharez, of the sons of Judah (1 Chr 9:4).

9.3.4.en: Imri: a Hebrew name, an abbreviation of Amariah. It is the name of a son of Bani of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr 9:4).

9.3.5.en: Bani: a Hebrew name, meaning "builder". Perhaps it is an abbreviation of "Benaiah", and he was of the tribe of Judah.

9.4.0.en: And of the Shilonites; Asaiah the firstborn, and his sons. [5]

9.4.1.en: Asaiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah has made". He was the firstborn of the Shilonite (1 Chr 9:5), and he was of the sons of Judah, and was living at the return from the captivity.

9.4.2.en: The Shilonites: the inhabitants of Shiloh. And of a family in Judah that dwelt in Jerusalem after the captivity (1 Chr 9:5).

9.5.0.en: And of the sons of Zerah; Jeuel, and their brethren, six hundred and ninety. [6]

9.5.1.en: Jeuel: a Hebrew name, meaning "he heals, he keeps". More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The father of Gibeon, a Benjamite among the forefathers of Saul (1 Chr 9:35). 2. A man of the descendants of Judah (1 Chr 9:6).

9.6.0.en: And of the sons of Benjamin; Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hasenuah [7]

9.6.1.en: Sallu: a Hebrew name, meaning "faithful forthwith, or consecrated". He was a man of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr 9:7).

9.6.2.en: Meshullam: a Hebrew name, meaning "one who has received his recompense". More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. Persons of the sons of Benjamin: Meshullam son of Hodaviah [7]; and Meshullam son of Shephathiah [8]. 2. One of the priests: Meshullam son of Zadok (1 Chr 9:11). 3. A priest of the family of Immer: Meshullam son of Meshillemith son of Immer (1 Chr 9:12).

9.6.3.en: Hodaviah: a Hebrew name, meaning "glory to Jehovah". He was the son of Hasenuah, of the sons of Benjamin (1 Chr 9:7).

9.6.4.en: Hasenuah: a Hebrew name, meaning "the hated". He was a man of Benjamin, the son of Hodaviah (1 Chr 9:7).

9.7.0.en: And Ibneiah the son of Jeroham, and Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri, and Meshullam the son of Shephathiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah; [8]

9.7.1.en: Ibneiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah builds". The son of Jeroham and the father of Reuel, of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr 9:8), and perhaps they are two persons.

9.7.2.en: Elah: a Hebrew name, meaning oak tree. He is the name of a son of Uzzi of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr 9:8).

9.7.3.en: Michri: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "price". He was a Benjamite, the grandfather of Elah (1 Chr 9:8).

9.7.4.en: Shephathiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah has given judgment". He was a Benjamite who dwelt in Jerusalem after the captivity (1 Chr 9:8).

9.7.5.en: Reuel: a Hebrew name, meaning "friend of God". He was a Benjamite chief (1 Chr 9:8).

9.8.0.en: And their brethren, according to their generations, nine hundred and fifty and six.

9.8.1.en: All these men were chief of the fathers in the house of their fathers. [9]

9.8.2.en: Perhaps the names mentioned here are of those who returned to Jerusalem and were occupied with the worship of God with burning zeal. The Temple had not yet been rebuilt, yet this did not lead them to neglect the worship of God.

9.9.0.en: 10 And of the priests; Jedaiah, and Jehoiarib, and Jachin, 11 And Azariah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of the house of God; 12 And Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashur, the son of Malchijah, and Maasiai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer; 13 And their brethren, heads of the house of their fathers, a thousand and seven hundred and threescore; very able men for the work of the service of the house of God.

9.9.1.en: And of the priests; Jedaiah, and Jehoiarib, and Jachin [10]

9.9.2.en: Jedaiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah knows".

9.9.3.en: Jehoiarib: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah contends, strives". He was of the descendants of Aaron, whose course was made the first of the courses of the priests in the days of David. His family dwelt in Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:10).

9.9.4.en: Jachin: a Hebrew name, meaning "he establishes". He was the head of the twenty-first course of the courses of the priests in Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:10).

9.10.0.en: And Azariah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of the house of God; [11]

9.10.1.en: Azariah: a Hebrew name, meaning "whom Jehovah has helped". He was the son of Hilkiah, and the father of Seraiah, and he was a great priest (1 Chr 9:11).

9.10.2.en: What occupies the heart of God is a person's faithfulness, not the kind of service or his position or his rank. Azariah received special attention although his role or work was to oversee the cleanliness of the Temple.

9.10.3.en: The Bible took care to mention his name in the genealogies as it took care to mention the names of the priests and Levites who carried out the works of teaching and praise and some positions of leadership which have an honoured appearance before people. God's esteem of man is not in his role in work or his position in society, but in the purity of his heart, his cleanness, his sincerity and faithfulness. Therefore the Lord's praise of those on the right hand on the great Day of the Lord: "You have been faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things: enter into the joy of your lord" (Mt 25:21).

9.10.4.en: Hilkiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah is my portion, my share".

9.10.5.en: Zadok: a Hebrew name, meaning "just or righteous". He was a priest of the line of the high priests, the father of Shallum and the son of the second Ahitub, of the second Meraioth (1 Chr 9:11).

9.10.6.en: Meraioth: "rebellion". He is the name of a priest, and he is the son of Ahitub (1 Chr 9:11).

9.10.7.en: Ahitub: a Hebrew name, meaning "brother of goodness".

9.11.0.en: And Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashur, the son of Malchijah, and Maasiai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer [12]

9.11.1.en: Adaiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "from the adornment of Jehovah". He was the son of Jeroham son of Malchijah, one of the priests (1 Chr 9:12).

9.11.2.en: Jeroham: a Hebrew name, meaning "he whom God has mercy upon or whom He pleases". He was a Benjamite, the father of Ibneiah, who was dwelling in Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:8). A priest of the house of Malchijah (1 Chr 9:10, 12).

9.11.3.en: Pashur: perhaps an Egyptian name meaning "portion of the god Horus". The founder of one of the families of the priests, some of whose members returned from the Babylonian captivity (1 Chr 9:12).

9.11.4.en: Malchijah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah is king".

9.11.5.en: Maasiai: a Hebrew name, meaning "work of Jehovah". He was a priest (1 Chr 9:12).

9.11.6.en: Adiel: a Hebrew name, meaning "adornment to God". He was the son of Jahzerah, the father of Maasiai, one of the heads of the priestly families (1 Chr 9:12).

9.11.8.en: Meshillemith: a Hebrew name, meaning "punishment". He was a priest of the line of Immer (1 Chr 9:12).

9.11.9.en: Immer: a Hebrew word meaning "sheep". The name of a priest in the age of David appears, and the sixteenth course of the priests was of his descendants. Perhaps he was the forefather of the priests mentioned in (1 Chr 9:12).

9.12.0.en: And their brethren, heads of the house of their fathers, a thousand and seven hundred and threescore; very able men for the work of the service of the house of God. [13]

9.12.1.en: They were mighty men of valour not in fighting nor in material resources, but in their seriousness in serving the house of the Lord and resisting error. We are accustomed to hear of "mighty men of valour" for entering into battles with enemies to overcome them, but here the heads of their fathers' houses are required to be mighty men of valour for the work of the service of the house of God. As if the house of God were a battlefield, and it befits the servants of God to be mighty men of valour who stand against the devil himself and the powers of darkness.

9.13.0.en: 14 And of the Levites; Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari; 15 And Bakbakkar, Heresh, and Galal, and Mattaniah the son of Micah, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph; 16 And Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun, and Berechiah the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, that dwelt in the villages of the Netophathites.

9.13.1.en: The Levites practiced praise or singing with exact arrangement and order, as there were 24 courses for this work. Praise was not a job from which the singers made a living, but a worship issuing from hearts consecrated to the Lord and sanctified to Him, whose message is to give an experience of the pledge of the heavenly life. The Levite singers were fathers who offered the people a life of joy and exultation, finding their happiness in the happiness of the people in God, the source of joy.

9.13.2.en: And of the Levites; Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari. [14]

9.13.3.en: Shemaiah: it means "Jehovah hears". He is a Levite of the descendants of Burni. He was overseer of the outward business of the house of God in the days of Nehemiah (1 Chr 9:14).

9.13.4.en: Hasshub: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "he who is thought of, or toward whom God's thought turns". A Merarite Levite, the father of Shemaiah (1 Chr 9:14).

9.13.5.en: Azrikam: a Hebrew name, meaning "my help has risen". More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The son of Azel, one of the descendants of Jehonathan son of Saul (1 Chr 9:44). 2. The son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari, a Levite (1 Chr 9:14).

9.13.6.en: Hashabiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah has devised or reckoned". Perhaps he was of the descendants of Buni, mentioned as an ancestor of Shemaiah (1 Chr 9:14).

9.14.0.en: And Bakbakkar, Heresh, and Galal, and Mattaniah the son of Micah, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph; [15]

9.14.1.en: Bakbakkar: a Hebrew name, meaning "searcher". He was a Levite man (1 Chr 9:15).

9.14.2.en: Heresh: a Hebrew name, meaning "dumb, deaf". The head of a Levite clan, attached to the officers of the tabernacle in 445 BC (1 Chr 9:15).

9.14.3.en: Galal: a Hebrew name, meaning "the Lord has rolled". He was a Levite (1 Chr 9:15). More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. A Levite (1 Chr 9:15). 2. A second Levite (1 Chr 9:16).

9.14.4.en: Mattaniah: a Hebrew name, meaning "gift of Jehovah". He was a Levite singer of the sons of Asaph (1 Chr 9:15).

9.14.5.en: Micah: a Hebrew name, meaning "Who is like Jehovah?" More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The son of Mephibosheth or Meribaal, and grandson of Jonathan (1 Chr 9:40-41). 2. A Levite, son of Zichri or Zabdi son of Asaph (1 Chr 9:15).

9.14.6.en: Zichri: a Hebrew name, meaning "remembered". He was a Levite (1 Chr 9:15).

9.14.7.en: Asaph: a Hebrew name, meaning "brother of Manah" or "gift". He was one of the Levites, gatekeepers of the Temple, and in his charge was the guarding of the east gate by which the king entered (1 Chr 9:15, 17).

9.15.0.en: And Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun, and Berechiah the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, that dwelt in the villages of the Netophathites. [16]

9.16.0.en: Most of those returning from the captivity of the priests and Levites dwelt in Jerusalem [34], but some of them were found who dwelt in the villages, perhaps because they did not find a place for themselves in Jerusalem.

9.16.1.en: Obadiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "festival (servant) of Jehovah". More than one person bears this name, among them: 1. The son of Azel, of the descendants of Jehoshaphat son of Saul (1 Chr 9:44). 2. The son of Shemaiah, of the descendants of Elkanah, who dwelt in the villages of the Netophathites (1 Chr 9:16). 3. A Levite, one of the gatekeepers of the Temple in the days of Nehemiah the governor (Neh 11:17; 12:25). Perhaps he was the same Obadiah son of Shemaiah (1 Chr 9:16).

9.16.2.en: Jeduthun: a Hebrew name, meaning "praising, one who praises". He was a Levite, and one of the three great singers or musicians whom David appointed, and the founder of a musical family for worship in the Temple. Jeduthun's course was in the Temple after its completion, and also after the captivity (1 Chr 9:16).

9.16.3.en: Berechiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "blessed of God". He was a Levite, the son of Asa (1 Chr 9:16).

9.16.4.en: Asa: a Hebrew name, meaning "the healer", that is, "the physician". Perhaps the name is an abbreviation of "Jehovah healed", that is, "the Lord healed and cured". It is the name of a Levite, the son of Elkanah, who dwelt in the villages of the Netophathites after the return from the Babylonian captivity (1 Chr 9:16).

9.16.5.en: Elkanah: a Hebrew name, meaning "God has created or acquired". He was a Levite who dwelt in one of the villages of the Netophathites (1 Chr 9:16).

9.16.6.en: The Netophathites, Netophah: a Hebrew name meaning "munaffit". It is a town in Judah near Bethlehem (1 Chr 2:54; Neh 7:26), and after the end of the captivity fifty-six of its inhabitants returned to it. At the beginning it was not of the portion of the Levites, but some of them dwelt in it after the captivity, as some singers dwelt in it (1 Chr 9:16).

9.16.7.en: And perhaps it was at Khirbet Bedd Falouh near Ain Netuf, to the south of Bethlehem by five generations.

9.17.0.en: 17 And the porters were, Shallum, and Akkub, and Talmon, and Ahiman, and their brethren: Shallum was the chief; 18 Who hitherto waited in the king's gate eastward: they were porters in the companies of the children of Levi. 19 And Shallum the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his brethren, of the house of his father, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the gates of the tabernacle: and their fathers, being over the host of the LORD, were keepers of the entry. 20 And Phinehas the son of Eleazar was the ruler over them in time past, and the LORD was with him. 21 And Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was porter of the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. 22 All these which were chosen to be porters in the gates were two hundred and twelve. These were reckoned by their genealogy in their villages, whom David and Samuel the seer did ordain in their set office. 23 So they and their children had the oversight of the gates of the house of the LORD, namely, the house of the tabernacle, to keep guard. 24 In four quarters were the porters, toward the east, west, north, and south. 25 And their brethren, which were in their villages, were to come after seven days from time to time with them. 26 For these Levites, the four chief porters, were in their set office, and were over the chambers and treasuries of the house of God. 27 And they lodged round about the house of God, because the charge was upon them, and the opening thereof every morning pertained to them.

9.17.1.en: The gatekeepers hold the place of precedence among the officials of worship [17-26]. Their offices go back to the time of the wilderness [19-21], and they continued their work in the days of Samuel and David in the tabernacle [23]. Their faithfulness is praised [22], and they are all of the line of Korah[2].

9.17.2.en: And the porters were, Shallum, and Akkub, and Talmon, and Ahiman, and their brethren: Shallum was the chief; [17]

9.17.3.en: Ahiman: a Hebrew name, meaning "brother of Manah or gift". He was one of the Levites, gatekeepers of the Temple, and in his charge was the guarding of the east gate by which the king entered (1 Chr 9:17).

9.18.0.en: Who hitherto waited in the king's gate eastward:

9.18.1.en: they were porters in the companies of the children of Levi. [18]

9.18.2.en: The keepers of the gates: they used to guard the four entrances of the Temple, and open the gates every morning for those entering for worship, and close them in the evening. They also carried out the daily works of preparing the Temple continually, such as cleaning and preparing the offerings for the sacrifices. They were also responsible that nothing unclean should enter the Temple, and they prevented those entering from behaving in a way not befitting the sanctity of the Temple. They also directed those entering the Temple to the required places. And they were entrusted with the storehouses of the Temple.

9.18.3.en: It befits all who work in the house of the Lord, whether in devotional, administrative or cleaning work, to be marked by sincerity and faithfulness.

9.19.0.en: And Shallum the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his brethren, of the house of his father,

9.19.1.en: the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the gates of the tabernacle: and their fathers, being over the host of the LORD, were keepers of the entry. [19]

9.19.2.en: The office of the gatekeepers and others in the service of the house of the Lord was inherited by the sons from the fathers. The beginning of this organization was in the reign of King David.

9.19.3.en: Kore: a Hebrew name, meaning "partridge". The name of a Korahite, the father of Shallum and Meshelemiah (1 Chr 9:19).

9.19.4.en: Ebiasaph: a Hebrew name, meaning "my father has gathered or increased".

9.19.5.en: Korah: a Hebrew name, meaning "terror". The descendants of Korah lived and became famous in the service of the Temple (1 Chr 9:19).

9.19.6.en: The Korahites: the descendants of Korah son of Izhar son of Kohath son of Levi, and among them were gatekeepers (1 Chr 9:31).

9.20.0.en: And Phinehas the son of Eleazar was the ruler over them in time past, and the LORD was with him. [20]

9.20.1.en: Phinehas: an Egyptian name meaning "the Nubian". He was the chief over the keepers of the gates of the tabernacle, he is Phinehas son of Eleazar, whose weapon was "the Lord is with him" [20].

9.20.2.en: He is most likely different from Phinehas the high priest, the son of Eleazar, who was zealous for the sanctity of the Temple (Num 25:7).

9.20.3.en: Eleazar: a Hebrew name meaning "God has helped".

9.21.0.en: And Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was porter of the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. [21]

9.21.1.en: Meshelemiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "whom Jehovah rewards". He was the father of a gatekeeper of the tabernacle of meeting in the days of David (1 Chr 9:21).

9.22.0.en: All these which were chosen to be porters in the gates were two hundred and twelve. These were reckoned by their genealogy in their villages.

9.22.1.en: Whom David and Samuel the seer did ordain in their set office. [22]

9.22.2.en: No one was permitted to be counted among the keepers of the Temple unless he was registered in the genealogical records proving that he was of the descendants of Abraham.

9.22.3.en: Although Samuel the prophet died before David was installed as king, it is clear that he took part in arranging the worship, though this is not mentioned in another place.

9.23.0.en: So they and their children had the oversight of the gates of the house of the LORD, namely, the house of the tabernacle, to keep guard. [23]

9.23.1.en: The priests and Levites devoted much time and effort to worship, with care for many of the instruments of the service. And their families did many works so that worship might be practiced "decently and in order" (1 Cor 14:40). All worked so that the people, when they came to worship, would feel that they were meeting the King of kings in preparation worthy of Him.

9.24.0.en: In four quarters were the porters, toward the east, west, north, and south. [24]

9.24.1.en: Many of the Levites worked as gatekeepers, keeping guard [23] at the gates and entrances. King David longed to stand with them, saying: "For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness" (Ps 84:10).

9.25.0.en: And their brethren, which were in their villages, were to come after seven days from time to time with them. [25]

9.25.1.en: The gatekeepers used to relieve one another on the Sabbath, so one group went and another group took its place. They lived in their villages until the time of their turn of service came, and then they came to Jerusalem.

9.26.0.en: For these Levites, the four chief porters, were in their set office, and were over the chambers and treasuries of the house of God. [26]

9.27.0.en: And they lodged round about the house of God, because the charge was upon them, and the opening thereof every morning pertained to them. [27]

9.28.0.en: 28 And certain of them had the charge of the ministering vessels, that they should bring them in and out by tale. 29 Some of them also were appointed to oversee the vessels, and all the instruments of the sanctuary, and the fine flour, and the wine, and the frankincense, and the spices. 30 And some of the sons of the priests made the ointment of the spices. 31 And Mattithiah, one of the Levites, who was the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, had the set office over the things that were made in the pans. 32 And other of their brethren, of the sons of the Kohathites, were over the shewbread, to prepare it every sabbath.

9.28.1.en: And certain of them had the charge of the ministering vessels, that they should bring them in and out by tale. [28]

9.28.2.en: They brought in the vessels by count, because they were very precious (Ezra 8:24-34).

9.29.0.en: Some of them also were appointed to oversee the vessels, and all the instruments of the sanctuary, and the fine flour, and the wine, and the frankincense, and the spices. [29]

9.30.0.en: And some of the sons of the priests made the ointment of the spices. [30]

9.31.0.en: And Mattithiah, one of the Levites, who was the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, had the set office over the things that were made in the pans. [31]

9.31.1.en: Mattithiah: a Hebrew name, meaning "gift of Jehovah". It is the name of a Korahite Levite, appointed over the work of the cooked things (1 Chr 9:31).

9.31.2.en: Shallum: a Hebrew name, meaning "recompense". The chief of the gatekeepers of the sanctuaries (1 Chr 9:17-18). He was the son of Kore. He and his family worked in guarding the sanctuaries (1 Chr 9:19).

9.31.3.en: One of the members of the family of the high priests who were of Zadok, and a predecessor of Ezra. He lived before the siege of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar. He is the one called "Meshullam" in (1 Chr 9:11).

9.32.0.en: And other of their brethren, of the sons of the Kohathites, were over the shewbread, to prepare it every sabbath. [32]

9.32.1.en: They used to remove the old bread on the Sabbath day, and put the new (Lev 24:8).

9.33.0.en: 33 And these are the singers, chief of the fathers of the Levites, who remaining in the chambers were free: for they were employed in that work day and night. 34 These chief fathers of the Levites were chief throughout their generations; these dwelt at Jerusalem.

9.33.1.en: And these are the singers, chief of the fathers of the Levites, who remaining in the chambers were free: for they were employed in that work day and night. [33]

9.33.2.en: They were exempt from other work, or from tribute, or military service.

9.33.3.en: There was a company or several courses for praising God, not for a few minutes or hours in the day, but praising God by day and night. These were great leaders, heads of the families of the Levites. The service of praise is not a secondary service, but an essential work, which raises the people as well as the leaders to the heavenly angelic service. Therefore it befits that it be practiced not as a kind of amusement or entertainment, but as a living encounter with God whom the heavenly orders praise.

9.34.0.en: These chief fathers of the Levites

9.34.3.en: The singers were fully devoted to the work day and night, dwelling in Jerusalem. So praise was a perpetual work, to give a joyful heavenly atmosphere.

9.35.0.en: 35 And in Gibeon dwelt the father of Gibeon, Jehiel, whose wife's name was Maachah: 36 And his firstborn son Abdon, then Zur, and Kish, and Baal, and Ner, and Nadab, 37 And Gedor, and Ahio, and Zechariah, and Mikloth. 38 And Mikloth begat Shimeam. And they also dwelt over against their brethren in Jerusalem, with their brethren. 39 And Ner begat Kish; and Kish begat Saul; and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Esh-baal. 40 And the son of Jonathan was Merib-baal: and Merib-baal begat Micah. 41 And the sons of Micah were, Pithon, and Melech, and Tahrea, and Ahaz. 42 And Ahaz begat Jarah; and Jarah begat Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri begat Moza; 43 And Moza begat Binea; and Rephaiah his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son. 44 And Azel had six sons, whose names are these, Azrikam, Bocheru, then Ishmael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan: these were the sons of Azel.

9.35.1.en: And in Gibeon dwelt the father of Gibeon, Jehiel, whose wife's name was Maachah: [35]

9.35.2.en: We note that what is stated here [35-44] reveals commitment to order and decency in the service of the house of the Lord (1 Cor 14:40).

9.35.3.en: The writer returned to the genealogies of Saul in order to prepare for the battle of Gilboa [1000 BC] at the beginning of the next chapter. David took the throne through Saul's death in this battle.

9.35.4.en: Gibeon: a Hebrew name, meaning "hill", the main city of the Hivites of the people of Canaan. And after several centuries, when Saul killed the Gibeonites, justice was exacted from his seven sons, and they were hanged. Gibeon became of the portion of Benjamin. It was also given with its pasture lands to the sons of Aaron. And the ancestors of Saul dwelt there for a time, and they had influence (1 Chr 9:35).

9.35.5.en: Maachah: a Semitic name, meaning "injustice". She was the wife of Jeuel the father of Gibeon, from whom Saul descended (1 Chr 9:35).

9.36.0.en: And his firstborn son Abdon, then Zur, and Kish, and Baal, and Ner, and Nadab [36]

9.36.1.en: Abdon: a Hebrew name, meaning "the enslaved". He was a Benjamite, son of Jeuel the Gibeonite (1 Chr 9:36).

9.36.2.en: Zur: a Semitic name, meaning "rock". He was the son of the founder of Gibeon (1 Chr 9:36).

9.36.3.en: Baal, the Baal, and its plural Baalim: a Semitic name, meaning "lord or master or husband". He was a Canaanite god, and was the son of the god El and husband of the goddess Baalah or Asherah or Anath or Ashtoreth, and is known as the god Hadad. He was the god of the farms and lord of fertility in the fields and among the animals and cattle.

9.36.4.en: Ner: a Hebrew name, meaning "light, lamp". He was a Benjamite, the son of Jeuel and Maachah and the father of Kish the father of Saul (1 Chr 9:35-36).

9.36.5.en: Nadab: a Hebrew name, meaning "generous". He was a son of Jeuel, and his mother's name was Maachah. He was of the sons of Benjamin. He lived in Gibeon, and he was the head of his house (1 Chr 9:36).

9.37.0.en: And Gedor, and Ahio, and Zechariah, and Mikloth. [37]

9.37.1.en: Gedor: a Hebrew name, meaning "fortress or walled place". He was the son of Jeuel, and the brother of Ner and Kish, of the ancestors of Saul (1 Chr 9:35-37).

9.37.2.en: Mikloth: a Hebrew name, meaning "staff". It is the name of a Benjamite (1 Chr 9:37-38).

9.38.1.en: And they also dwelt over against their brethren in Jerusalem, with their brethren. [38]

9.38.2.en: Shimeam: a Benjamite, he was the son of Mikloth, living in Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:38).

9.39.0.en: And Ner begat Kish; and Kish begat Saul; and Saul begat

9.39.1.en: Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Esh-baal. [39]

9.39.2.en: Jonathan: a Hebrew name, meaning "Jehovah has given".

9.39.3.en: Malchishua: a Hebrew name, meaning "the king is salvation".

9.39.4.en: Abinadat: a Hebrew name, meaning "the father is generous or delegated".

9.39.5.en: Esh-baal: a Hebrew name, meaning "man of Baal". It is the first name of Ishbosheth son of Saul (2 Sam 2:8).

9.40.0.en: And the son of Jonathan was Merib-baal: and Merib-baal begat Micah. [40]

9.40.1.en: Merib-baal: also called Mephibosheth, a Hebrew name meaning "removal of idols".

9.41.0.en: And the sons of Micah were, Pithon, and Melech, and Tahrea, and Ahaz. [41]

9.41.1.en: Melech: a Hebrew name, meaning "king". He was the son of Micah, grandson of Mephibosheth (1 Chr 9:41).

9.41.2.en: Tahrea: a Hebrew name, meaning "crafty". He was a man of the descendants of Saul through Jonathan (1 Chr 9:41).

9.41.3.en: Ahaz: a Hebrew name, meaning "he held," that is, "the Lord held". He was Ahaz son of Micah, of the descendants of Jonathan (1 Chr 9:42).

9.42.0.en: And Ahaz begat Jarah; and Jarah begat Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri;

9.42.2.en: Jarah: a Hebrew name, meaning "honeycomb". He was a man of the descendants of Saul (1 Chr 9:42).

9.42.3.en: Azmaveth: a Hebrew name, meaning "death is strong". He was the son of Jehoadah, and one of the grandsons of Jehonathan son of Saul, and it is stated in (1 Chr 9:42) that this Azmaveth is the son of Jarah.

9.42.4.en: Zimri: a Hebrew name, perhaps meaning "he who resembles the wild ox", and he was a Benjamite of the descendants of Jonathan son of Saul (1 Chr 9:42).

9.42.5.en: Alemeth: a Hebrew name, meaning "concealment". He was the son of Jehoadah, of the sons of Benjamin. He was of the grandsons of King Saul (1 Chr 9:42).

9.43.0.en: And Moza begat Binea; and Rephaiah his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son. [43]

9.43.1.en: Moza: a Hebrew name, meaning "exit". It is the name of a man of the descendants of Saul (1 Chr 9:42-43).

9.43.2.en: Yina: this name appeared in the original and in most translations in the form "Binea". He was the son of Moza, of the descendants of Jonathan son of Saul (1 Chr 9:43).

9.43.3.en: Eleasah, Elasah: a Hebrew name meaning "God has made". It is the name of a man of the descendants of Saul and of his son Jonathan (1 Chr 9:43). His name appeared in the text in the form "Alasah".

9.44.0.en: And Azel had six sons, whose names are these:

9.44.1.en: Azrikam, Bocheru, then Ishmael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan:

9.44.2.en: these were the sons of Azel. [44]

9.44.3.en: Bocheru: a Hebrew name, meaning "firstborn". He was a son of Azel (1 Chr 9:44).

9.44.4.en: Ishmael: a Hebrew name, meaning "God hears". He was a Benjamite called Ishmael son of Azel (1 Chr 9:44).

9.44.5.en: Sheariah: a Hebrew name, meaning "power of Jehovah". A man of the descendants of Saul (1 Chr 9:44).

9.44.6.en: Hanan: a Hebrew name, meaning "gracious, compassionate, generous". He was a son of Azel, of the descendants of Jonathan son of Saul (1 Chr 9:44).

9.44.7.en: My heart and my flesh cry out for the living God

9.44.8.en: v My God, my sins and the sins of my fathers have spoiled the joy of the Spirit in the community as in my heart.

9.44.9.en: By returning to You and cleaving to Your word, You restore to me more than I had lost, and You bring me and my brethren into the pledge of heaven.

9.44.10.en: v Let me return from the captivity of sin to the Jerusalem above, and enjoy with my brethren union with You.

9.44.11.en: It does not concern me whether I am one of the people, or a priest or one of the Levite singers, or a keeper of the gates of Your holy house.

9.44.12.en: For all together become like a near-heavenly order.

9.44.13.en: Our hearts together with our bodies cry out to You, O living God.

9.44.14.en: You pour Your holiness upon all, O Sanctifier of all.

9.44.15.en: Your Holy Spirit works in all.

9.44.16.en: So that we bear the mark of faithfulness and sincerity!

9.44.17.en: Truly we become members of Your body, O Son of David!
